- **Status:** DONE — task commit `8ad6a7b`, merged to `master` as `138c3d0` with `--no-ff` on 2026-09-17; pushed by the user the same day (the agent's own `git push` was refused by the auto-mode classifier as *Out-of-Place Publication*). **Runtime VERIFIED live 2026-09-17, signed out:** `/Login` and `/LOGIN` both answer `302 Location: /login` — note the **`callbackUrl` is gone**, which is the observable signature of the new guard firing ahead of the auth branch rather than after it — and both chains terminate at `200` in a single hop, so the loop the first conjunct guards against does not occur. `www.therapyjo.com/Login` reaches the same place in two hops. **Regression surface re-measured and intact:** `/login` still `200` with `X-Matched-Path: /login`; `/admin` signed out still `302 → /login?callbackUrl=%2Fadmin`, so callbackUrl is still minted for genuinely protected routes; `/Login.aspx` still `307 → /clinic/Login.aspx`; `/clinic/` still `200` with `X-Powered-By: ASP.NET`; `/clinic` still `307 → /clinic/`. **One bullet remains unobserved rather than passed:** the signed-in `/Login` path, because no agent can hold a clinic session. It is the same guard on the same line, firing before the auth branch, so it redirects to `/login` and the pre-existing `pathname === "/login" && isLoggedIn` rule forwards to the role dashboard — reasoned, not measured, and recorded as such.
- **Branch:** `bugfix/canonicalise-login-case`
- **Why:** Clinic staff open the dashboard from a bookmark reading `https://therapyjo.com/Login` — capital `L`, carried over from years of the legacy ASP.NET `Login.aspx`. Next.js routing is case-sensitive and this app only has `/login`, so `/Login` matches no route and serves Next's built-in 404. There is no `not-found.tsx` anywhere in `src/app`, which is why the screen the clinic photographed is the unstyled "404 | This page could not be found." **Two distinct code paths reach it**, which is why it presents as intermittent rather than constant:
  1. **Already signed in.** `authorized()` in `src/lib/auth.config.ts` compares `pathname === "/login"` exactly, so `/Login` is not recognised as the login page, is not matched by `publicRoutes`, does not trip `!isLoggedIn`, and does not start with `/admin`, `/secretary` or `/doctor`. The callback falls all the way through and returns `true`; the request is allowed into routing and nothing matches.
  2. **Signed out.** The callback redirects to `/login?callbackUrl=%2FLogin`, the form renders, the credentials work — and then `src/app/login/page.tsx` reads that `callbackUrl` and, because `"/Login".includes("/login")` is `false`, navigates the user to `/Login`. They are dumped on the 404 *after* a successful sign-in.
- **Measured against production 2026-09-17**, not inferred: `/login` → `200` with `X-Matched-Path: /login` and `X-Nextjs-Prerender: 1`; `/Login` signed out → `302 Location: /login?callbackUrl=%2FLogin`; `https://www.therapyjo.com/Login` → `308` to the apex **with the capital L preserved**; `/Login.aspx` → `307 Location: /clinic/Login.aspx` (already handled, not part of this bug). When this lands, every case variant of the login path resolves to the real login page, and a signed-in visitor is forwarded to their role dashboard as usual.

**Planning pass:** 2026-09-17 — read `src/lib/auth.config.ts` in full, `src/app/login/page.tsx` lines 1–75, `src/middleware.ts` in full, and `next.config.mjs` in full. Confirmed `src/app/admin/page.tsx`, `src/app/secretary/page.tsx`, `src/app/doctor/page.tsx` and `src/app/login/page.tsx` all exist, so the post-sign-in destinations are sound and the login path is the only broken one. Confirmed `callbackUrl` has exactly one reader (`src/app/login/page.tsx:36`) and one writer (`src/lib/auth.config.ts:64`); the three `signOut({ callbackUrl: "/login" })` call sites pass a hard-coded lowercase literal and are unaffected.

**Corrected the assumption this task started from:** that a plain refresh of `/Login` recovers. It does not. A signed-in refresh of `/Login` 404s again, because the guard that lets it through is auth-state-independent. What actually recovers the clinic is re-entering the URL — Chrome autocompletes the lowercase `/login` already in history — or pressing Back to `/login?callbackUrl=…`, where a now-signed-in user is forwarded to their dashboard. **Do not write a verification bullet that expects a same-URL refresh to pass on today's code.**

**Confirmed the fix cannot collide with the legacy proxy.** Next's routing order is headers → redirects → middleware → `beforeFiles` rewrites → filesystem, so `/Login.aspx` is consumed by `redirects()` in `next.config.mjs` and never reaches middleware, and `/clinic/` is excluded by the middleware matcher. ### TJ-053 — One Arabic-capable font for the site's text

- **Status:** DONE — task commit `a96a37c`, merged to `master` as `d9a53ee` with `--no-ff` on 2026-09-28 at the user's request; **live check owed after the Vercel deploy.** Before the merge this read: REVIEW — implemented as `a96a37c` on `claude/festive-brown-n77ft7`, 2026-09-28; see the review block below. Not yet merged to `master`. **The claim that English headings "keep Bodoni Moda" was wrong: they never had it (TJ-055).** **User decision, 2026-09-28: option A, IBM Plex Sans Arabic.** Execute with `FONT_IMPORT` = `IBM_Plex_Sans_Arabic` and the A options row (the `weight` array is required). This exact option was dry-run in the planning pass: type-checked, built and measured, then reverted.
- **Branch:** `feat/arabic-body-font`
- **Why:** User request, 2026-09-28: change the font of the site's text, "most importantly" to one suited to Arabic.

  **Today's body font, Inter, has no Arabic glyphs at all.** Its next/font subsets are cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, greek-ext, latin, latin-ext and vietnamese. The only Arabic face, Noto Kufi Arabic, applies only under `[dir="rtl"]`, i.e. after a visitor switches the public site to Arabic.

  Everywhere else, Arabic glyphs fall to the next face in the stack. That's next/font's `Inter Fallback`, which the built CSS defines as `src: local(Arial)` with a size adjustment and no `unicode-range`. So Arabic renders in Arial where Arial is installed, and in the platform's own sans elsewhere. It never renders in a face this site chose, and it looks different from machine to machine. That covers:
  - **Every staff screen.** Admin, secretary and doctor pages are LTR only and never set `dir="rtl"`, and they use `font-family: inherit` throughout. So every Arabic patient name, note and SOAP entry is in that fallback.
  - **The reviewer's name on an Arabic Google review on the English landing page.** `Reviews.tsx` renders it with `dir="auto"`, which flips the direction but not the font. The quote itself is a separate case; see the known leftover below.
  - **Arabic blog drafts in the admin editor.** `BlogEditor.tsx` sets `dir` to `rtl` on the body `<textarea>`, but `<html>` stays `ltr`, so the `[dir="rtl"] body` rule never matches.

  Separately, Kufi is a geometric display style. It's strong for headings but tiring for paragraphs and small UI text, which is most of this site.

**Planning pass:** 2026-09-28. Read:
- `src/app/layout.tsx` in full
- every `font-family`, `--font-*` and `[dir="rtl"]` rule in `src/app/globals.css`
- `src/app/i18n/LanguageContext.tsx`
- the typography section of `design_handoff_landing_and_blog_cms/README.md`
- the next/font catalogue and type signatures that ship with `next@16.1.6`

Also tallied every `font-weight` in `src/`.

Confirmed:
- **The font variables have exactly these consumers**, per `grep -rn "font-inter\|font-arabic\|'Inter'\|Noto Kufi" src`:
  - `--font-inter`: `body` in `globals.css`
  - `--font-arabic`: `[dir="rtl"] body`, `[dir="rtl"] { --font-heading }` and `.lang-toggle`

  No component names a font directly except the Outfit wordmark. Every staff page follows `body` through `inherit`, so they need no per-file change.
- **Weights in use:** 600 ×175, 500 ×60, 700 ×54, 400 ×11, 800 ×2. The two 800s are `.reviews-rating-number` in the heading font and the Outfit wordmark on `/unauthorized`. A candidate must have 400, 500, 600 and 700, or every semibold label silently turns bold. **That rules out Tajawal (no 600) and Almarai (no 500 or 600)**, two otherwise popular choices.
- **Italics** appear only in `--font-heading`, which is Bodoni Moda in English. Arabic has no italic, so no candidate needs one.
- **English headings are unchanged.** The design handoff specifies Bodoni Moda for English display headings and Outfit for the wordmark. This task changes body text in both languages and Arabic headings. If the user also wants English headings in the new face, that's a one-line follow-up to `--font-heading` in `:root`, not part of this task.
- **Schedule cards don't get wider.** Names ellipsize at the narrowest schedule column, 110px (TJ-049a), so a wider face would truncate sooner. Width at the card's own size (12.8px bold), measured in Chromium with the real font files:

  | Face | "Mohammad Al-Khatib" | "محمد عبد الرحمن الخطيب" |
  |---|---|---|
  | Today | 137px (Inter) | 154px (Noto Kufi Arabic) |
  | IBM Plex Sans Arabic | 131px | 137px |
  | Readex Pro | 140px | 154px |
  | Cairo | 122px | 141px |
  | Noto Sans Arabic | 139px | 145px |

  Every candidate is within 2% of today or narrower.
- **Card heights can't move.** `body` sets `line-height: 1.6`, and every staff element inherits it. The line box is fixed by font size, not by each face's own vertical metrics.
- **The fallback behaviour was read from the built CSS**, not assumed. The baseline build emits:
  - `--font-serif:"Bodoni Moda","Bodoni Moda Fallback"`, with `Bodoni Moda Fallback` defined as `src: local(Times New Roman)`
  - `Inter Fallback` and `Noto Kufi Arabic Fallback`, both defined as `src: local(Arial)`

  None of the fallback faces has a `unicode-range`, so each one catches any glyph its local font has. **Corrected during this pass:** Latin text on the Arabic site is *not* in Arial today. next/font declares every subset's `@font-face` (it only *preloads* the ones listed), so Noto Kufi's latin face serves those characters on demand.

**Known leftover, not fixed here.** Arabic set in the *heading* font while the page is English will still fall back after this task. English headings keep Bodoni Moda, which has no Arabic, and its `Times New Roman` fallback face catches Arabic glyphs before any later family in the stack could. In practice this affects one element: an Arabic Google review's quote (`.reviews-quote-text`, set in `var(--font-heading)`). Two ways to fix it, each a separate small task:
- Load Bodoni Moda with `adjustFontFallback: false` and add `var(--font-body)` to the `:root` `--font-heading` stack.
- Set the quote in the body face.

**Options — the user picks one.** All four ship Arabic and Latin in one family, loaded with `subsets: ["arabic", "latin"]`. So a mixed line, such as an Arabic name beside a Latin phone number, renders in one design. Payload is the woff2 for both subsets as served by Google Fonts on 2026-09-28. For comparison, today's Inter + Noto Kufi Arabic is 168 KB for the same job.

| | Font | Character | Weights | Files / KB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** *(recommended)* | IBM Plex Sans Arabic | Clinical and precise. Arabic and Latin drawn as one family; compact. | 100–700, static | 8 / 251 KB |
| **B** | Readex Pro | Friendly, open, rounded-geometric. Closest to the Project Profile's "Rounded Modern"; built for ease of reading. | 160–700, variable | 2 / 53 KB |
| **C** | Cairo | The most familiar Arabic web face in the region; compact Latin. | 200–1000, variable | 2 / 63 KB |
| **D** | Noto Sans Arabic | Naskh style: the classic Arabic reading texture, best for long paragraphs. | 100–900, variable | 2 / 192 KB |

The `next/font` call for each, in the formatting used by step 2:

| | Import name | Options object |
|---|---|---|
| A | `IBM_Plex_Sans_Arabic` | `subsets: ["arabic", "latin"]`, `weight: ["400", "500", "600", "700"]`, `variable: "--font-body"`, `display: "swap"`. `weight` is **required** here, because next/font's signature for a static family demands it. |
| B | `Readex_Pro` | `subsets: ["arabic", "latin"]`, `variable: "--font-body"`, `display: "swap"` |
| C | `Cairo` | `subsets: ["arabic", "latin"]`, `variable: "--font-body"`, `display: "swap"` |
| D | `Noto_Sans_Arabic` | `subsets: ["arabic", "latin"]`, `variable: "--font-body"`, `display: "swap"` |

**Why A.** The site's heaviest reading happens on the staff dashboards: names, times, phone numbers and notes at 11–13px. Plex was designed for exactly that kind of dense interface, in both scripts. Its Latin is close to Inter, so the English side barely changes character, while Arabic finally gets a proper face everywhere.

Its cost is weight. A static family needs one file per weight, so the page preloads 10 font files instead of 4. **Measured in the dry-run build:**
- Preloaded fonts: 4 files / 224 KB → 10 files / 249 KB (+25 KB).
- All emitted fonts: 18 files / 536 KB → 22 files / 330 KB. Noto Kufi's many unicode-range slices go away.

Pick B or C if payload matters more than tone.

### TJ-054 — Doctors: no patient phone numbers, and no patient edits beyond clinical work and files

- **Status:** SPLIT. Re-planned 2026-09-28 after the user's decisions (below). See TJ-054a, TJ-054b, TJ-054c and TJ-054d. **All four were implemented in order on `claude/festive-brown-n77ft7` on 2026-09-28, runtime-proven against a local database** (see "Measured after the change"), **and merged to `master` as `d9a53ee`.**

**Live check owed after the deploy.** No agent holds a clinic login, so the doctor-side bullets can be confirmed only by someone who does. On production, as a doctor:
- no phone on schedule cards, the patient list, the patient page or the session page
- no Add Patient, Edit Info, Archive or file-Remove control
- a search by a known number still finds the patient

As a secretary, everything is unchanged. Nothing executes against this ID.
- **Why:** Two user directives, both 2026-09-28:
  1. Limit doctors' access to patient information, so that "they can't view patient's mobile numbers".
  2. Doctors "can no longer edit patient info other than adding the clinical assessment or files". They also lose the ability to create new patients and to archive.

  One carve-out, from the same message: doctors **can still search by number**. "If they have the number they can search for it." The search result gives them the patient's name, never the number back.

**The rule, as decided by the user on 2026-09-28:**

| A doctor may… | Today | After TJ-054 |
|---|---|---|
| see a patient's `phone1` / `phone2` anywhere | yes | **no** |
| search patients by a number they already hold | yes | **yes**; the match returns the name only |
| register a new patient | yes | **no** |
| edit a patient's name, phones or photo | yes | **no** |
| archive or restore a patient | yes | **no** |
| fill in and update the Clinical Assessment (intake) | yes | yes |
| attach a file to a patient | yes | yes |
| remove a file from a patient | yes | **no**. The user permitted *adding* files, so removal counts as an edit. The user may reverse this one line. |
| write SOAP notes, change session status, set a session's injury place, duplicate a session | yes | yes; these are session records, not patient details |

**Admins and secretaries are unaffected.** Both new rules are keyed to the signed-in role, so an admin who opens a `/doctor/*` page still sees and can do everything. Other patient data a doctor sees (session payment type, photo, "Last updated by") was offered to the user for hiding and **not** requested, so it stays visible.

**Measured before the change.** This ran against a local Postgres 16 (SSL on, as `src/lib/prisma.ts` requires), with `prisma db push`, fixture users of all three roles, two patients, two sessions and one file. The app was a `next build` + `next start` of commit `58467b0`, and requests were made with real NextAuth credential sessions. As DOCTOR:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/patients`, `?search=<phone>`, `/api/patients/1` | 200, `phone1` and `phone2` present |
| `GET /api/patients/duplicates` | 200 |
| `GET /api/reservations?date=`, `?patientId=`, `/api/reservations/1` | 200, `patient` = `id,name,phone1,phone2` |
| `PATCH` / `PUT /api/reservations/1`, `POST …/duplicate` | 200/200/201, response `patient` includes `phone1` |
| `POST /api/patients` | **201**: the doctor created a patient |
| `PUT /api/patients/1` | **200**, and the response carried both phones |
| `PATCH /api/patients/1` `{archived:true}` | **200 "Patient archived"** |
| `DELETE /api/patients/1/files/1` | **200 "File removed"** |

**Two server-side rules, each named once in `src/lib/permissions.ts`** beside `canAccessClinical`, for the reason that file already gives: one predicate, used at every call site.
- `canManagePatients` (ADMIN or SECRETARY) covers: registering a patient, changing their details, archiving or restoring them, and removing their files.
- `canViewPatientContact` (ADMIN or SECRETARY) covers: whether a response carries `phone1` / `phone2`.

**Split** into four tasks to respect the four-file cap and keep each diff to one concern:

| Task | Concern | Files |
|---|---|---|
| a | doctor screens | 3 edited + 1 deleted |
| b | server: who may change a patient | 4 |
| c | server: phones, patient routes | 4 |
| d | server: phones, reservation routes + the schedule card | 4 |

**Why the order.**
- **a before b:** a removes the doctor's Add Patient, Edit Info, Archive and file-Remove controls. Otherwise b would leave four buttons that answer 403.
- **c needs b:** c appends its helper after b's in `permissions.ts`.
- **d needs c:** d imports c's helper.
- **d carries the card change:** it includes `ReservationSlot.tsx`, so the schedule card stops drawing a phone in the same commit that stops the server sending one.

Every intermediate state is safe. The one hazard in the first plan (the doctor's Edit Info modal re-posting `phone2: ""` and blanking a patient's second number) is gone, because a removes the modal and b refuses the write.

**Measured after the change, 2026-09-28.** This used the same database recipe and the same probe script as the "before" table, run against a production build of `c8ee974`: 39 probes across all three roles.

As DOCTOR:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/patients` | 200, no `phone1` or `phone2` key |
| `GET /api/patients?search=0799819669` | 200, **the patient is found**, no phone key |
| `GET /api/patients/1` | 200, no phones, `intake` present, `files` present |
| `GET /api/patients/duplicates` | **403** |
| `GET /api/reservations?date=` and `?patientId=` | 200, `patient` = `id,name` |
| `GET /api/reservations/1` | 200, `patient` = `archived,id,name`, `soapNote` present |
| `GET /api/reservations?month=` | 200, counts unchanged |
| `POST /api/patients` | **403** "Not permitted to register patients" |
| `PUT /api/patients/1` | **403** "Not permitted to edit patients" |
| `PATCH /api/patients/1` (archive) | **403** "Not permitted to edit patients" |
| `DELETE /api/patients/1/files/1` | **403** "Not permitted to remove patient files" |
| `PUT /api/patients/1/intake` | 200 |
| `POST /api/patients/1/files` | 201 |
| `PATCH`, `PUT /api/reservations/1` | 200, response `patient` = `id,name` |
| `POST /api/reservations/1/duplicate` | 201, response `patient` = `id,name` |
| Raw bodies of all eight doctor GETs above | contain **none** of the fixture phone strings |

As SECRETARY, unchanged:
- `PUT` with a phone change → 200
- archive → 200, restore → 200
- register → 201
- remove a file → 200
- phones present on every read
- `intake` and `soapNote` still absent (TJ-023 holds)

As ADMIN, everything is present, duplicates → 200, and patient 1's phones and archived flag are unchanged after the doctor's attempts.

**Gates:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` exits 0.
- `npm run build` exits 0.
- ESLint on every changed source file gives **4 errors before and 4 after**, all the existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on the fetch idiom, in the same four files, measured in a clean baseline worktree.


**All-roles check, 2026-09-28**, on a fresh fixture database against the final build (`41ee5ad`). Each role was signed in through the real login form and checked on its own screens:

| | Admin | Secretary | Doctor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dashboard font (body and card names, incl. the Arabic name) | IBM Plex Sans Arabic | IBM Plex Sans Arabic | IBM Plex Sans Arabic |
| Date-picker surface (TJ-052) | `rgb(238, 244, 246)` | `rgb(238, 244, 246)` | `rgb(238, 244, 246)` |
| Schedule cards | phone and "·" shown | phone and "·" shown | **no phone, no "·"** |
| Patient list | Phone column and Add control | Phone column and Add control | **no Phone column, no Add control** |
| Patient page: phones shown | 2 | 2 | **0** |
| Patient page: Edit Info / Archive / file Remove | yes / yes / 1 | yes / yes / 1 | **no / no / 0** |

The 39 API probes were also re-run on the fresh database, and their output is **byte-identical** to the "Measured after the change" run above.

- **Status:** DONE — task commit `da2d4cf`, merged to `master` as `d9a53ee` with `--no-ff` on 2026-09-28; **live check owed.** Before the merge this read: implemented as `da2d4cf`, 2026-09-28; runtime-proven (see TJ-054); not yet merged.

Confirmed:

- **The search's `OR` clauses on `phone1` / `phone2` stay as they are**, per the user: a doctor may find a patient by a number they hold. The number is not selected into the response, so the match returns the name only.
- **`PUT /api/patients/[id]` needs no `omit`.** After TJ-054b only an admin or a secretary can reach its response.
- **`POST /api/patients` needs no change.** After TJ-054b a doctor can't reach it, so its 409 (which quotes a stored number) is served only to staff who may see numbers.
- **`GET /api/patients/duplicates` is called only by admin pages.** Refusing doctors breaks no screen.

**Scope — touch only these:**
- `src/lib/permissions.ts`
- `src/app/api/patients/route.ts` (`GET` only)
- `src/app/api/patients/[id]/route.ts` (`GET` only)
- `src/app/api/patients/duplicates/route.ts`

**Instructions:**
1. Append `canViewPatientContact` (ADMIN or SECRETARY) to `permissions.ts`. Its doc comment should state that a doctor may search by a number but is never sent one.
2. `GET /api/patients`: compute `const contact = canViewPatientContact(session.user);` and select `phone1: contact, phone2: contact`. Leave the search `OR` untouched.
3. `GET /api/patients/[id]`: compute `contact` beside `clinical`, and add `omit: { phone1: !contact, phone2: !contact }` to the `findUnique`.
4. `GET /api/patients/duplicates`: immediately after the 401 check, refuse with 403 `"Not permitted to view patient phone numbers"` when `!canViewPatientContact(session.user)`.

**Verification:**

Static: tsc and build pass.

Runtime:
- As a doctor:
  - the list, the search by phone, and the single record carry no `phone1` or `phone2` key
  - a search by a patient's number still finds that patient
  - `intake` is still present (TJ-023's doctor half)
  - duplicates → 403
- As a secretary: phones are present and `intake` is absent (TJ-023 unchanged).
- As an admin: everything is present, and duplicates → 200.

**Done when:**
- [x] No patient route sends a doctor a phone
- [x] A doctor's search by number still finds the patient
- [x] Admin and secretary responses are unchanged
- [x] tsc and build pass

- **Status:** DONE — task commit `32bd05c`, merged to `master` as `d9a53ee` with `--no-ff` on 2026-09-28 at the user's request; **live check owed after the Vercel deploy.** Before the merge this read: REVIEW — implemented as `32bd05c` on `claude/festive-brown-n77ft7`, 2026-09-28; see the review block at the end of this task. Not yet merged to `master`. **Decision, 2026-09-28: the user said "whatever you recommend"; the planner chose option 2**, keeping headings in the body face.
- **Branch:** `bugfix/heading-font-variable`
- **Why:** `globals.css` declares `--font-heading` in two places:
  - on `:root`, as `var(--font-serif), 'Bodoni Moda', serif`
  - under `[dir="rtl"]` (i.e. on `<html>`), as `var(--font-body), sans-serif`

  But `layout.tsx` puts every next/font variable class on **`<body>`**, so `--font-serif` and `--font-body` exist only from `<body>` down. A custom property that references an undefined variable is invalid at computed-value time. So `--font-heading` computes to nothing on `<html>`, and `<body>` inherits that nothing. Every `font-family: var(--font-heading)` rule then falls back to the inherited body font. There are 18 of these in `globals.css`, including section titles, the hero title, section labels, the marquee, the review quote and footer headings.
- **Measured on a local build of `a96a37c`:**
  - `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--font-heading')` is `""`, and the same on `<body>`.
  - `--font-serif` is `"Bodoni Moda","Bodoni Moda Fallback"` on `<body>` and `""` on `<html>`.
  - `.section-title` computes to the body stack.
  - An isolated page, `:root{--h:var(--x),serif} body{--x:"Courier New"} .t{font-family:var(--h)}`, renders `.t` in the inherited body font. That's the mechanism, independent of this app.
- **What that means:**
  - English headings have been Inter, never the Bodoni Moda the design handoff specifies. Since TJ-053 they are IBM Plex Sans Arabic.
  - Arabic headings were meant to use the body face anyway, so they're unaffected in practice.
  - **Bodoni Moda is still downloaded on every page for nothing.** next/font preloads its latin face, `52b5d5098cb87ddd-s.p.cd0f0e4b.woff2` (25 KB), and no element renders in it.
- **Decision for the user:**
  1. **Restore Bodoni Moda for English headings, as designed.** Likely fix: move the `${x.variable}` classes from `<body>` to `<html>` in `layout.tsx`, which is next/font's documented placement, so `:root` can see them. That's one file, but a *visible* change: English headings become the serif for the first time.
     - The TJ-053 known leftover then becomes real: an Arabic Google review quote would fall to `Bodoni Moda Fallback` (`local(Times New Roman)`). So fix it in the same task, either by loading Bodoni with `adjustFontFallback: false` and adding `var(--font-body)` to the `:root` stack, or by setting `.reviews-quote-text` in the body face.
  2. **Keep headings in the body face** and delete the dead indirection instead: remove `Bodoni_Moda` from `layout.tsx` and point `--font-heading` at `var(--font-body)`. This saves the 25 KB preload.
- **Found** while reviewing TJ-053 in a real browser, 2026-09-28. The planning pass had read the CSS and assumed the variable resolved. It was the computed style that showed it didn't.

**Why option 2.**
- It's the look the live site has always had. English headings have been sans since launch, Inter and now IBM Plex, and nobody noticed the missing serif.
- It honours the user's TJ-053 choice of one face for both languages. Bodoni has no Arabic, so it could only ever style half the site.
- It removes a 25 KB preload that every page paid for nothing.
- It avoids the Times New Roman fallback that restoring Bodoni would have created for Arabic review quotes.

Option 1 remains available later as a deliberate redesign.

**Planning pass:** 2026-09-28. Read `src/app/layout.tsx` in full and every `--font-*` and `font-family` declaration in `src/app/globals.css`.
- `--font-serif` and `Bodoni` appear only in `layout.tsx` and in the `:root` `--font-heading` line.
- `font-family: var(--font-heading)` appears 18 times.
- Apart from those, the only `font-family` declarations are `body`, `.lang-toggle` and two `inherit`s, so no heading sits inside a container with its own face.
- The only other font-variable consumers are the Outfit wordmark (`admin/layout.tsx`, `login/page.tsx`, `unauthorized/page.tsx`) and `.lang-toggle`. They inherit from `<html>` just as well as from `<body>`.

**Scope:** `src/app/layout.tsx` and `src/app/globals.css`.

**The change:**
- In `layout.tsx`, drop `Bodoni_Moda` (import, `const`, class) and move the remaining `${x.variable}` classes from `<body>` to `<html>`, with a comment saying why.
- In `globals.css`, set `:root` `--font-heading` to `var(--font-body), sans-serif`, and delete the `[dir="rtl"]` block, which is now identical.

**Planner review, 2026-09-28: passed; not yet merged.**
- **Gates:** `tsc` exits 0, and `npm run build` exits 0. ESLint on `layout.tsx` is clean.
- **Fonts emitted:** preloaded goes from 10 files / 249 KB to **9 files / 223 KB**, and all fonts from 22 files / 330 KB to 18 files / 256 KB.
- **Measured before (`8445ea2`) and after (`32bd05c`)** on a local `next start`, in English and Arabic, for every heading selector on `/`. That's 12 of the 18: the doctor, blog and review selectors need data the fixture doesn't have, and they use the same rule.
  - `--font-heading` goes from `""` to `"IBM Plex Sans Arabic","IBM Plex Sans Arabic Fallback",sans-serif`.

### TJ-056 — Card text reads blurry on Windows: unhinted font files and faded muted lines

- **Status:** DONE — task commit `2079d78`, merged to `master` as `220ed3e` with `--no-ff` on 2026-09-28 at the user's request. **Owed:** a look at the live dashboard on a Windows machine, the only place the gain is visible.
- **Branch:** `bugfix/windows-text-rendering`
- **Why:** User report, 2026-09-28, with a screenshot of the live dashboard: "the font still kinda looks blurry". The screenshot's own pixels were measured rather than guessed at. Each antialiased text pixel was compared against the straight line from the card colour to the ink colour; greyscale smoothing stays on that line, and ClearType leaves colour fringes off it.

  | Line in the screenshot | Mean offset from the line (0–765 scale) |
  |---|---|
  | Name line, on yellow and on green cards | 43.6 / 43.5 → **ClearType**, so the machine is Windows |
  | Phone/time line, same cards | 0.9 / 0.8 → **greyscale** |

  Two causes follow.
  1. **`opacity` on the muted lines.** `.slot-sub` is at 0.8, and `.slot-time` at 0.85 inside it (0.68 overall); the separator and note are faded the same way. Chrome turns off ClearType for text drawn with opacity below 1, which is exactly the split measured above. This predates TJ-053. The new face made it more visible.
  2. **Unhinted font files.** next/font/google fetches with a Mac user agent (`fetch-resource.js`), and Google serves Macs unhinted files. Measured on the Google CSS2 files:

     | | Hinting tables | Glyphs with instructions |
     |---|---|---|
     | Mac UA (what the build shipped) | `gasp` only | 0 |
     | Windows UA | `fpgm`, `prep`, `cvt `, `gasp` | 434 Arabic, 188 Latin |

     All 16 IBM Plex files in the TJ-053/055 build had no hinting. Windows needs hinting to grid-fit 11–13px text. The Arial it replaced for Arabic is fully hinted.

**Planning pass:** 2026-09-28. Read `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/components/ReservationSlot.tsx` and next/font's `fetch-resource.js`.
- `@ibm/plex-sans-arabic@1.1.0` on npm is IBM's own release, licensed OFL-1.1. Its `fonts/complete/woff2` files are **hinted**: `fpgm`, `prep` and `cvt `, with 711–851 instructed glyphs per weight. Each carries Arabic and Latin in a single file.
- The files are copied in, not added as a dependency, so `package.json` is unchanged.
- **Exception to the "existing directories only" rule:** new directory `src/app/fonts/ibm-plex-sans-arabic/`. next/font/local resolves paths relative to `layout.tsx`, and `public/` would also serve the files raw at a second URL.
- **`color-mix(in srgb, currentColor N%, var(--slot-bg))` gives the same shade the old opacity did.** Compositing is linear in sRGB, so it is the same blend, just opaque. `.slot` sets `--slot-bg` inline from the doctor colour. A malformed doctor colour makes the mix invalid, and the text then inherits full colour, which is still readable.
- **Not touched:** `.menu-trigger` (0.7, an icon, not text) and a checked-out card's whole-card `opacity: 0.5`, which is deliberate dimming.

**Scope:** `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/components/ReservationSlot.tsx`, and new files `src/app/fonts/ibm-plex-sans-arabic/{Regular,Medium,SemiBold,Bold}.woff2` plus `LICENSE.txt`.

**Review, 2026-09-28:**
- **Gates:** `tsc` exits 0, `npm run build` exits 0, and ESLint is clean on both files.
- **Fonts:** all 4 shipped IBM Plex files carry `fpgm` / `prep` / `cvt `. Preloaded fonts go from 9 files / 223 KB to **5 files / 322 KB** (+99 KB, four fewer requests).
- **Runtime**, local `next start` against the fixture database, as a secretary and as a doctor:
  - all four `bodyFont` weights are `loaded`
  - on a `#93c5fd` card, `.slot-sub` computes to `color(srgb 0.1969 0.2988 0.3647)`, which is exactly 80% ink over the card colour
  - `.slot-time` computes to 0.68 of ink, identical to the old combined opacity
  - every muted line reports `opacity: 1`
  - doctor cards still carry no phone and no separator
- **Owed, and only a Windows machine can give it:** a look at the same dashboard after deploy. Headless Chromium on Linux renders greyscale either way, so the ClearType and hinting gain can't be seen here. It is expected from how Windows renders, not observed.
- **Offered, not done:** IBM Plex draws its Arabic small for its size. The same Arabic name is 137px wide where Noto Kufi was 154px. A `size-adjust` of about 110% on the Arabic range would bring it back up, but it would also re-flow the Arabic public site, so it's a design decision for the user.

### TJ-057 — Draw Arabic 10% larger; clip long Arabic names at their end

- **Status:** DONE — task commit `e60699e`, merged to `master` as `01cfb82` with `--no-ff` on 2026-09-28 at the user's request. **Owed:** a look at the live site and dashboard on a Windows machine.
- **Branch:** `feat/arabic-size-adjust`
- **Why:** User request, 2026-09-28, taking up the option offered in TJ-056. IBM Plex sets its Arabic small for its size: the same name is 137px where Noto Kufi drew 154px, which costs legibility on 11–13px schedule cards.

**Planning pass:** 2026-09-28. Read `src/app/layout.tsx`, the `:root` font block of `src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/components/ReservationSlot.tsx`, the next/font/local option types, and next's `next-font-loader` (`index.js`, `postcss-next-font.js`).
- **`declarations` works as documented.** next/font/local accepts it and writes it into each generated `@font-face`, so `unicode-range` and `size-adjust` can be set on a second rule that uses the same files.
- **Corrected mid-pass, measured:** switching the fallback setting off on only the Arabic rule made next/font emit a second copy of every file. It names files `[hash]{-s}{.p}` by those flags, and `-s` is the fallback flag. Preloads went to 9 files / 613 KB. Mirroring the base rule's options gives identical file names, so the browser fetches each file once.
- **The trap that mirroring creates:** the fallback setting generates a `Fallback` face (`local(Arial)`, no `unicode-range`). If the Arabic rule's full variable sat in the stack, that face would catch Latin text ahead of the base face. So only the Arabic rule's own family name is taken, via `arabicFont.style.fontFamily`, and `--font-body` is set inline on `<html>`. `:root` keeps `--font-body: var(--font-body-base)` as an unscaled fallback.
- **The range covers the Arabic blocks only:** U+0600–06FF, 0750–077F, 0870–08FF, FB50–FDFF, FE70–FEFF, plus U+200C–200D. ZWNJ/ZWJ must shape in the same face. Digits and punctuation are left out on purpose, so they stay unscaled.
- **Found during the check:** with the larger letters, one long name in the narrowest column ("عبدالله ابو السخن", 122px) now overflowed, and it clipped its **first** word. The name span inherits the card's LTR direction. That was already true for long enough names; the larger letters just made it happen sooner. The fix: `dir="auto"` on `.slot-name`, so an Arabic name clips its last word instead, with `text-align: left` keeping every name at its old edge.

**Scope:** `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/globals.css` and `src/app/components/ReservationSlot.tsx`.

**Review, 2026-09-28**, on a local build against the fixture database, with ten more Arabic-named sessions at 12:00 so the columns pack narrow:
- **Gates:** `tsc` exits 0, `npm run build` exits 0, and ESLint is clean.
- **Generated CSS:** four `arabicFont` faces, each with the range and `size-adjust:110%`. `<html>` carries `--font-body:'arabicFont', var(--font-body-base)`, with no fallback face between them.
- **Preloads:** 5 files / 322 KB, the same as before this task.
- **Measured before and after:**

  | Measure | Before | After |
  |---|---|---|
  | Arabic phrase at 16px | 109px | **119px** |
  | Latin phrase at 16px | 157px | **157px** (unchanged) |
  | Arabic site line counts (hero title, hero subtitle, About title) | 2 / 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 / 2 |
  | Arabic site page height | 7350px | 7379px |
  | Card height | 64px | 64px |
  | Arabic names clipped in the narrowest column (122px) | 0 of 11 | 1 of 11, now at its end ("عبدالله ابو السـ…") |

  Horizontal overflow at 1440px is still none. The overflow at 320px was already there and is unchanged.
- **All-roles check:** admin, secretary and doctor all render cards in the new stack. Phones show for admin and secretary and not for the doctor. The date picker is still Mist, and patient controls are unchanged per role.
- **Owed:** a look on a Windows machine after deploy, the same as TJ-056.

### TJ-059 — Ten more calendar colours for doctors

- **Status:** DONE. Passed planner review and QA on 2026-10-12. Task commit `34270bf` on `feat/more-doctor-colours`, merged into `claude/exciting-einstein-krgpmv` as `aa47fca` with `--no-ff`. Merged to `master` with `--no-ff` as `7622d50` on 2026-10-12, at the user's request. **Live check owed:** no agent can reach or sign in to production.
- **Branch:** `feat/more-doctor-colours`
- **Why:** User request, 2026-10-12: "add more color options to assign to doctors, add about 10 more." There are 12 colours, and TJ-009d made each one exclusive to a single ACTIVE doctor, so the 13th active doctor already has to share one ("Every colour is in use — this one will be shared"). Ten more makes 22.

**Planning pass:** 2026-10-12. Files read:
- `src/app/admin/employees/doctors/page.tsx`: `COLORS`, `takenColors`, `paletteExhausted`, the edit modal's picker and its CSS.
- `src/app/admin/employees/doctors/new/page.tsx`: `COLORS`, TJ-009h's first-free default, the picker and its CSS.
- The colour handling in `src/app/api/employees/doctors/route.ts` and `.../doctors/[id]/route.ts`.
- `src/app/components/ReservationSlot.tsx`: `readableTextColor`, `STATUS_COLORS`, the checked-out opacity.
- The `User.color` and `Reservation.doctorColorSnapshot` columns in `prisma/schema.prisma`, and `prisma/seed.ts`.

Findings:
- **Confirmed: the palette is two identical literal arrays and nothing else.** A `diff` of the two `COLORS` blocks is empty, and no other file lists colours. The server keeps no whitelist. It only refuses a colour that another ACTIVE doctor holds, by exact string. The schema stores any string. Every consumer treats the value as opaque: the calendar card, the snapshot and the table dot. Adding values needs no change to the server, the schema or the data.
- **Confirmed: the picker logic scales on its own.** `paletteExhausted` and the "every colour is in use" fallbacks compare against `COLORS.length`. TJ-009h's default takes the first free colour in array order. The new values are **appended**, so:
  - the first 12 keep their positions;
  - `COLORS[0]` stays `#6ee7b7`;
  - every doctor's saved colour still matches a swatch, which the edit modal needs to show it selected.
- **How the ten were chosen.** A card is filled with the doctor's colour, and `readableTextColor` gives it either white or `#1a2e35` text, whichever contrasts more. Candidates were Tailwind's 200–500 shades, the family the existing 12 come from (all 300/400). A candidate had to pass three tests:
  - text contrast of at least 4.5:1 under that rule (the existing palette's floor is 5.11);
  - contrast against the dashboard background of at least 3:1;
  - CIELAB chroma of at least 35, so it reads as a colour.

  Greys were excluded. A grey card reads as "inactive", it collapses into the background at the checked-out 50% opacity, and `#666` is already the deleted-doctor fallback. From what was left, each next pick was the candidate farthest, by CIEDE2000, from everything already in the palette:

  | Added, in array order | Tailwind | Card text | Text contrast | Nearest colour, ΔE₀₀ |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `#fda4af` | rose-300 | dark | 7.47 | 10.5 (pink-300) |
  | `#fdba74` | orange-300 | dark | 8.38 | 10.8 (orange-400) |
  | `#fef08a` | yellow-200 | dark | 12.14 | 11.3 (lime-200) |

### TJ-060 — Sign in with a username in any case

- **Status:** DONE. Passed planner review and QA on 2026-10-12. Task commit `61b10e3` on `feat/username-any-case`, merged into `claude/exciting-einstein-krgpmv` as `72afb3e` with `--no-ff`. Merged to `master` with `--no-ff` as `7622d50` on 2026-10-12, at the user's request. **Live check owed:** no agent can reach or sign in to production.
- **Branch:** `feat/username-any-case`
- **Why:** User request, 2026-10-12: "make the username not case sensitive at sign in." `authorize()` finds the account with `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { username } })`, which is an exact, case-sensitive match. So `dr.ahmad` typed for an account stored as `Dr.Ahmad` is refused as a wrong password. The usual cause is a phone capitalising the first letter. Once this lands, a username signs in in any case, and the password check stays exactly as strict as it is.

**Planning pass:** 2026-10-12. Files read:
- `src/lib/auth.ts` in full, `src/lib/auth.config.ts`, the imports of `src/middleware.ts`, and `src/lib/prisma.ts`.
- The `User` model in `prisma/schema.prisma`, and `prisma/seed.ts`.
- The `POST` and `PUT` handlers of `src/app/api/employees/doctors/route.ts`, `.../doctors/[id]/route.ts`, `.../secretaries/route.ts` and `.../secretaries/[id]/route.ts`.
- The username fields of the four employee pages, and `src/app/login/page.tsx`.

Findings:
- **Confirmed: usernames are written in two places only, the two `POST` routes.** Both `PUT` handlers destructure the body without `username`, so a username cannot change after creation. The edit modals hide the field outside the Add mode nobody can reach. Each `POST` guards with an exact `findUnique` and answers 409 "Username already taken". The seed creates the first admin from `ADMIN_USERNAME`.
- **Confirmed: `username` is `@unique` and case-sensitive.** It is a Postgres `text` column, with no `citext` and no functional index. Two accounts that differ only by case can exist today, so a case-blind lookup can return more than one row. The design below says what happens then.
- **Corrected, by measurement: the obvious fix turns `%` into a wildcard at the login box.** Prisma's `equals` with `mode: "insensitive"` was run against a local Postgres 16 with Prisma 7.4.1, with query logging on. It compiles to `WHERE "username" ILIKE $1` and **escapes nothing**:
  - Input `fif%` matched the account `fifty%`.
  - Input `%` matched **every** account.
  - Inside `authorize()`, `%` would therefore try the password against whichever account the database returned first. Every wrong guess would add to a random colleague's lockout counter.
  - It also fails the other way. `\` is `ILIKE`'s escape character, so an account whose username contains one could never sign in.
  - Filtering the `ILIKE` rows in JavaScript fixes the wildcard but not the backslash.
- **Chosen instead: `SELECT id FROM "User" WHERE lower(username) = lower(${input})`.** It goes through Prisma's tagged `$queryRaw`, in one small helper shared by all three call sites.
  - Run against the same inputs, it gives the exact answer every time, backslash included.
  - The tag binds the input as `$1`. `x' OR '1'='1` and `'; DROP TABLE "User"; --` both returned 0 rows, and the query log showed `lower($1)` with the text passed as a parameter.
  - The table is `"User"`, since the schema has no `@@map`.
  - This is the repo's first raw query, which is why the helper's comment explains the choice.
- **Decided: a case collision never guesses.**
  - When exactly one account matches ignoring case, it signs in.
  - When several match, only the exact spelling signs in, which is exactly how those accounts behave today.
  - No new collisions can be created: both `POST` routes refuse a username that matches an existing one in any case, across roles.
- **Left out on purpose:**
  - Trimming whitespace: `"dr.ahmad "` is still refused, as today.
  - `autoCapitalize="none"` on the login input.
  - Rewriting stored usernames to lower case, which would need a write to production rows and could collide on the unique index.
  - The seed's exact `findUnique`, which an operator runs once.
- **Prototyped and runtime-proven.** In a throwaway worktree, `tsc` exits 0 and `npm run build` exits 0. Lint is unchanged at 64: the new file and the three edited ones have no findings.

  The test ran against a local Postgres seeded with `Admin`, `Dr.Ahmad`, `dr_sami` and a deliberate collision pair, `secA` / `SECA`. Sign-in went through the real `POST /api/auth/callback/credentials`, and the result was read back from `/api/auth/session`:

  | Typed | Password | Signed in as |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Dr.Ahmad` | right | Dr.Ahmad (the exact-case control) |
  | `dr.ahmad` | right | Dr.Ahmad |
  | `DR.AHMAD` | right | Dr.Ahmad |
  | `dr_sami` | right | dr_sami |
  | `DR_SAMI` | right | dr_sami |
  | `dr.ahmad` | wrong | refused |
  | `%` | Dr.Ahmad's | refused |
  | `%` | wrong | refused |
  | `dr%` | Dr.Ahmad's | refused |
  | `secA` | secA's | secA |
  | `SECA` | SECA's | SECA |
  | `seca` | secA's | refused (collision, neither spelling exact) |
  | `Seca` | SECA's | refused (collision, neither spelling exact) |
  | `dr.ahmad ` (trailing space) | right | refused (not trimmed, as today) |

  Failed-attempt counters afterwards: `Dr.Ahmad=1`, from the one wrong password, on the right account. Every other account was at `0`, so **the two `%` attempts moved no one's counter.**

  Creating accounts as `admin` (itself signed in in lower case):

  | Route | Username | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | `POST /api/employees/doctors` | `DR.AHMAD` | 409 "Username already taken" |
  | `POST /api/employees/secretaries` | `dr.ahmad` | 409 (across roles) |
  | `POST /api/employees/secretaries` | `seca` | 409 |
  | `POST /api/employees/doctors` | `Dr.Ahmad` | 409 (exact duplicate, as today) |
  | `POST /api/employees/doctors` | `new_doc%` | 201 |
  | `POST /api/employees/doctors` | `NEW_DOC%` | 409 |

  `New_Doc%` then signed in as the account created as `new_doc%`.
- **A harness trap, recorded so the executor does not chase it.** `src/lib/prisma.ts` always connects with SSL. A local Postgres therefore has to run with `ssl=on`; a self-signed certificate is enough. Without it, every sign-in fails with `CallbackRouteError … The server does not support SSL connections`, which looks exactly like the feature not working. The exact-case control row above is what tells the two apart.

**Scope — touch only these:**
- `src/lib/username.ts` (new; `src/lib` exists)
- `src/lib/auth.ts`
- `src/app/api/employees/doctors/route.ts` (`POST` only)
- `src/app/api/employees/secretaries/route.ts` (`POST` only)

**Do not touch:**
- `src/lib/auth.config.ts` and `src/middleware.ts`. They run on the Edge and must stay free of Prisma, so the helper is imported only from `auth.ts` and the route handlers.
- The `[id]` `PUT` routes, since usernames cannot change.
- `prisma/schema.prisma`. There is no migration and no `db push`. Stored usernames keep the case they were created with, and the admin tables keep showing it.
- `prisma/seed.ts` and `src/app/login/page.tsx`.
- The rest of `authorize()`. The status check, the lockout and its counters stay exactly as they are, applied to whichever account the lookup resolves.

**Instructions.** All files are LF. Each anchor below occurs exactly once in its file (machine-checked 2026-10-12).

**Step 1.** Create `src/lib/username.ts` with exactly:
```ts
import "server-only";
import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";

/**
 * The ids of every account whose username equals `input`, ignoring case.
 *
 * Raw SQL on purpose. Prisma's `mode: "insensitive"` compiles to a bare
 * `ILIKE $1` with nothing escaped (measured on Prisma 7.4.1), so a `%` or
 * `_` typed at the login box acts as a wildcard — `%` alone matches every
 * account — and a username containing `\` can never match itself.
 * `lower() = lower()` is plain equality with none of that. The template tag
 * binds `input` as a parameter; it is never spliced into the SQL. (TJ-060)
 */
export async function findUserIdsByUsername(input: string): Promise<string[]> {
    const rows = await prisma.$queryRaw<{ id: string }[]>`
        SELECT id FROM "User" WHERE lower(username) = lower(${input})
    `;
    return rows.map((r) => r.id);
}
```

**Step 2.** In `src/lib/auth.ts`, replace:
```ts
import { authConfig } from "@/lib/auth.config";
```
with:
```ts
import { authConfig } from "@/lib/auth.config";
import { findUserIdsByUsername } from "@/lib/username";
```

**Step 3.** In `src/lib/auth.ts`, replace:
```ts
                const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
                    where: { username: credentials.username as string },
                });
```
with:
```ts
                // A username signs in in any case: a phone that capitalises
                // the first letter must not shut anyone out. Should two
                // accounts ever differ only by case, only the exact spelling
                // signs in — never a guess between two people. (TJ-060)
                const typed = credentials.username as string;
                const ids = await findUserIdsByUsername(typed);
                const user = ids.length === 1
                    ? await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: ids[0] } })
                    : await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { username: typed } });
```
The second branch covers both zero matches and a collision. With zero matches the exact lookup finds nothing either. With a collision it finds only the exact spelling. Keep it as a ternary rather than `let user = null` plus an `if`: under this repo's `"strict": false`, `let user = null` widens to `any` and drops the typing of every check below it.

**Step 4.** In `src/app/api/employees/doctors/route.ts`, replace `import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";` with that line followed by `import { findUserIdsByUsername } from "@/lib/username";`. Then replace:
```ts
    // Check if username is taken
    const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { username } });
```
with:
```ts
    // Taken in any case: sign-in ignores case, so "Dr.Ahmad" beside an
    // existing "dr.ahmad" would be two accounts behind one login. (TJ-060)
    const existing = (await findUserIdsByUsername(username)).length > 0;
```

**Step 5.** In `src/app/api/employees/secretaries/route.ts`, add the same import line in the same way. Then replace:
```ts
    const existing = await prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { username } });
```
with:
```ts
    // Taken in any case: sign-in ignores case, so "Sec.Rana" beside an
    // existing "sec.rana" would be two accounts behind one login. (TJ-060)
    const existing = (await findUserIdsByUsername(username)).length > 0;
```
In both routes, the `if (existing) {` line that follows stays as it is. `existing` is now a boolean.

- `npm run lint` reports `64 problems (50 errors, 14 warnings)`, unchanged.
- `grep -c findUserIdsByUsername` returns `2` in `src/lib/auth.ts`, `2` in each of the two routes, and `1` in `src/lib/username.ts`.
- `grep -rn "insensitive" src/lib/auth.ts src/app/api/employees | wc -l` returns `0`. The phrase does appear in `username.ts`'s comment on purpose, so grepping that file returns `1`.

- `git diff --stat master` lists exactly the four files. `auth.config.ts` and `middleware.ts` are unchanged.

### TJ-062 — Limit doctors to their own sessions

- **Status:** SPLIT, **complete**. Passed 2026-10-12, with every decision taken, and split into **TJ-062a** (server) and **TJ-062b** (screens). Both passed planner review and QA on 2026-10-12, tested together, and are merged into `claude/exciting-einstein-krgpmv` as `3a23dd6` and `7024348`, then to `master` as `7622d50` on 2026-10-12 at the user's request. **Live check owed.** Nothing executes against this ID.
- **Branch:** none of its own. TJ-062a is `feat/doctor-session-ownership` and TJ-062b is `feat/doctor-readonly-sessions`, both cut from `claude/exciting-einstein-krgpmv` at `3baee67`, after TJ-058 and TJ-061.
- **Why:** User request, 2026-10-12: nothing on the server stops a doctor changing status on, or writing notes for, a colleague's session. TJ-058 made colleagues' cards the first thing a doctor sees.

**Planning pass:** 2026-10-12. Files read:
- `src/app/api/reservations/[id]/route.ts` (`GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`), `.../soap/route.ts` and `.../duplicate/route.ts`.
- `src/app/api/patients/[id]/intake` (its call sites) and `src/lib/permissions.ts`.
- `src/app/doctor/session/[id]/page.tsx`: data loading and every save handler.
- The writes on `src/app/doctor/patients/[id]/page.tsx`.
- `src/app/api/notes/route.ts` and `.../notes/[id]/route.ts`, and the `Note` model.

Measured on `master`, signed in as `Dr.Ahmad`, acting on `dr_sami`'s reservation:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET …/soap` (read the colleague's SOAP note) | 200 |
| `PUT …/soap` (write it) | **200** |
| `PATCH /api/reservations/<id>` `{ status: "CHECKED_IN" }` | **200**, and the status really changed |
| `PUT /api/reservations/<id>` `{ injuryPlace, paymentType }` | **200**, and the stored value changed |
| `PUT /api/patients/<id>/intake` (patient-level) | 200 |

- **Confirmed: no doctor-facing write checks ownership.**
  - `PATCH` (status) checks only that a session exists.
  - `PUT` refuses a doctor only for date, time and reassignment. Notes, injury, payment and the two-hour flag are open.
  - The SOAP `PUT` checks `canAccessClinical`, which is role-only.
  - Duplicate is TJ-061.
  - `DELETE` already refuses doctors.
- **Confirmed: ownership is checkable.** A reservation carries `doctorId`, and the session carries `session.user.id`. A reservation whose doctor was hard-deleted has `doctorId = null`, so no doctor owns it; admin can still act on it.
- **Confirmed: the intake is patient-level, not session-level.** One record per patient, shared by every doctor who treats them. Restricting it is a separate question from restricting sessions.
- **Adjacent, found during the pass:** `PUT /api/notes/[id]` lets any signed-in user, doctors included, edit any note, including reassigning its `doctorId`. Only `DELETE` refuses doctors. Not part of this request; listed as question 4.

**Decisions, 2026-10-12 (user):**
- **Q2: doctors may still read a colleague's sessions and SOAP notes** (the recommended option).
- **Q3: the patient-level intake stays shared** by every doctor (the recommended option).
- **Q1, answered later on 2026-10-12: status changes are blocked too.** A doctor changes nothing on a colleague's session: status, details and SOAP are all refused. Before that answer, Q1 had been narrowed as follows. The user asked what "details" meant. It means the non-clinical fields of one booked session that `PUT /api/reservations/[id]` lets a doctor change:
  - **on the doctor's screen**, injury place (the session page's "Save details");
  - **through the API only**, the calendar note and whether it shows on the card, the next-session note, the payment type, the two-hour flag and `isNote`.

  Date, time and reassignment are already refused to doctors. SOAP and details are blocked under either answer. **The open choice is only status:** may a doctor check in, mark waiting, move to "with doctor", check out or cancel a colleague's patient?
- **Q4, Notes editing,** has no recommendation on record yet. It is put to the user separately, and is not part of this task either way.

**Recommended design, pending the user's answers:**
- **Server:** a `canWriteSession(user, reservationDoctorId)` helper in `permissions.ts`. Admin and secretary keep exactly what they have. A doctor is allowed only when `reservationDoctorId === user.id`. It is applied to `PATCH` and `PUT /api/reservations/[id]` and to the SOAP `PUT`, and to Duplicate if TJ-061 chooses option B. A refusal is a 403 naming the rule.
- **UI:** on the doctor dashboard, a colleague's card shows no status actions. The session page opens a colleague's session read-only: a banner naming the doctor, and no save or status buttons. Without this the server change alone would leave buttons that fail.

**The decisions, for the user:**
1. **Which writes on a colleague's session are blocked?** Recommended: all of them (status, details, SOAP). The alternative is clinical writes only (SOAP and details), so any doctor can still move a colleague's patient through check-in and check-out.
2. **May a doctor still *read* a colleague's session and SOAP notes?** Recommended: yes, for continuity of care. TJ-058 already shows the cards.
3. **The patient-level intake:** keep it shared by every doctor (recommended), or restrict it to doctors who have a session with that patient?
4. **Should doctors' editing of Notes be limited too?** That would be a separate task.

```tsx
export function canViewPatientContact(
    user: Session["user"] | undefined | null
): boolean {
    if (!user) return false;
    return user.role === "ADMIN" || user.role === "SECRETARY";
}

/**
 * May this user change this session — its status, its details, or its SOAP
 * note?
 *
 * ADMIN and SECRETARY may change any session, as before. A DOCTOR may change
 * only a session booked under them: a colleague's session, and one whose
 * doctor was hard-deleted (doctorId null), are read-only to every doctor.
 * Reading is not restricted here — a doctor may still read a colleague's
 * session and SOAP note — and a secretary still may not touch a SOAP note
 * (canAccessClinical, checked separately). User decision, 2026-10-12. (TJ-062)
 */
export function canWriteSession(
    user: Session["user"] | undefined | null,
    sessionDoctorId: string | null
): boolean {
    if (!user) return false;
    if (user.role === "ADMIN" || user.role === "SECRETARY") return true;
    return user.role === "DOCTOR" && sessionDoctorId !== null && sessionDoctorId === user.id;
}
```

**Planning pass:** 2026-10-12. Files read:
- `src/app/components/ReservationSlot.tsx`: props, the action menu, the menu trigger and the render.
- `src/app/components/Calendar.tsx`: props, and the props passed to each slot.
- `src/app/doctor/page.tsx` after TJ-061.

Design:
- **Card:** `ReservationSlot` takes `readOnly`. A read-only card has **no ⋮ trigger**, so no menu at all. With TJ-061 a doctor has no Duplicate, Edit or Delete, so nothing useful is lost. A click on the card still opens the session, to read.
- **Calendar:** takes `ownerId`. When it is set, a card is read-only unless the reservation is booked under that id. Admin and secretary don't pass it, so they are unchanged.
- **Doctor dashboard:** `ownerId` is `undefined` for an admin, and otherwise the doctor's id, or `""` until the session loads. **That fails closed:** no card offers anything until the signed-in user is known.
- **Session page:** `readOnly = !me || (me.role === "DOCTOR" && reservation.doctor?.id !== me.id)`.
  - The header's status buttons, "Update Session" and "Save SOAP Note" are hidden.
  - Injury Place and the four SOAP fields become `readOnly`.
  - A "Read only" banner names the owner. It shows only once the user is known (`isColleagues`), so an owner never sees it flash during load. It reuses the previous-session-note banner's existing style.
  - **The Clinical Assessment tab stays editable** (decision Q3, the intake is shared). History is already read-only.

### TJ-063 — Staff are signed out, and cannot sign back in, while the database pooler is full

- **Status:** SPLIT, **complete**. Fixed live on 2026-10-26 by **TJ-063a** (`f3bf68d`). P4's results are recorded there, and P5 is done: `Production_Cutover.md` has been corrected in Hazard 8, the env table and *Declined, deliberately*. Nothing executes against this ID.
- **History:** Passed 2026-10-26. **P1 is measured** (below). **P2 and P3 are superseded:** the user asked the agents to do every step, the change needs the database password typed into Vercel, and an agent may not type a password. So the port switch moved into code, in **TJ-063a**, and needs no credential at all. P4 and P5 are the planner's, after TJ-063a deploys. Nothing executes against this ID.

**P1 result, measured 2026-10-26 in the Supabase dashboard (project `tqulxfdyfciwmqfmzlme`, read-only):**
- **Pooler logs, 25 Oct 11:00 to 26 Oct 12:00, search "max client": 71 entries, 14:34–14:35 on 25 Oct.** Every one reads `(EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max clients are limited to pool_size: 15`, some wrapped as `ECHECKOUTFAILED`.
- **Today's live traffic is session mode.** A `Connection authenticated` entry at 11:02:37 carries `mode: session`, user `postgres`, and peer `3.94.255.128`, an AWS `us-east-1` address, which is Vercel's `iad1`. It lines up with Vercel's request log at 10:59.
- **The Connect dialog** gives the session pooler as `postgresql://postgres.tqulxfdyfciwmqfmzlme:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@aws-1-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/`, and the transaction pooler as the **same string with port `6543`**.
- Project home: Postgres at **11/60** connections, compute Nano, no backups.
- **Vercel's logs could not show the incident.** Hobby keeps about 30 minutes of request logs, and that window held only `200`s.
- **Branch:** none of its own.
- **Why:** User report, 2026-10-26: during clinic hours, signing in to the admin dashboard is slow and then fails outright, and the logs say "max clients reached".

**Planning pass:** 2026-10-26. Files read:
- `src/lib/prisma.ts`, `src/lib/auth.ts`, `src/lib/auth.config.ts`, `src/lib/username.ts`, `src/middleware.ts`, `prisma.config.ts`, `.env.example`, `package.json`.
- `src/app/login/page.tsx`, `src/app/providers.tsx`, `src/app/SessionExpiryNotice.tsx`, the three dashboard layouts, and the data loading in `src/app/admin/page.tsx`.
- `GET` in `api/reservations/route.ts`, `api/employees/doctors/route.ts` and `api/patients/duplicates/route.ts`.
- Library code, at the installed versions: `pg-pool` 3.11.0 `index.js` (option defaults, the wait queue); `@prisma/adapter-pg` 7.4.1 `dist/index.js` (`performIO`, `startTransaction`); `@auth/core` 0.41.0 `lib/actions/session.js`; `next-auth` 5.0.0-beta.30 `lib/index.js` and `react.js`.
- `Production_Cutover.md`: the env table, *Declined, deliberately*, Hazard 8.
- The production build in `.next/server` (`BUILD_ID` `M0s2-mWbsTLphowNXH7dp`, built 2026-10-14).

**Confirmed: the cause.**

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| "max clients reached" is the **session-mode** pooler's error | Supavisor words it `(EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max clients are limited to pool_size`. Transaction mode words its own limit differently ("max client connections reached"), and that limit is 200. |
| Session mode caps the whole app at **15** | Pool size 15 at Nano (Hazard 8). In session mode a client keeps one of those 15 for as long as its connection is open, busy or idle. |
| Each instance holds up to **3** | `max: 3` in `prisma.ts`, and idle connections stay open for 10 s (`pg-pool`'s default `idleTimeoutMillis: 10000`). Five busy instances fill the cap. |
| One pool per instance, not one per route | The production build has exactly **one** server chunk that builds the pool. There is no duplicate-pool bug, and the `NODE_ENV` guard on the `globalThis` cache is harmless. |
| Production's port was never verified | *Declined, deliberately* in `Production_Cutover.md`: the owner said `6543`, recorded as "unverifiable". The error says `5432`. Local `.env` is on `5432` too. |

**Confirmed: why it shows up as a login failure, not just slowness.**

| Step | What the code does when the database cannot be reached |
|---|---|
| Waiting | `pg-pool` sets no `connectionTimeoutMillis` by default. A request waits in its queue with no limit, then in the pooler's queue until the pooler rejects it. **That is the latency.** |
| Session check | Every `auth()` and every `GET /api/auth/session` runs the `jwt` callback in `auth.ts`, which queries `User.status` (TJ-007). If that query throws, `@auth/core`'s session action catches the error and **clears the session cookie**, exactly as it does for a `null` return. |
| A tab comes back into view | **Two** session checks per staff tab. `SessionProvider` refetches on `visibilitychange` (`next-auth/react.js`, `refetchOnWindowFocus` defaults to true), and `SessionExpiryNotice.tsx` fetches `/api/auth/session` on the same event. On a full pool either one signs the person out, and they see "Your session has ended". |
| Signing back in | `authorize()` needs 2–3 queries. Any failure shows **"Invalid username or password"** (`login/page.tsx`, `if (result?.error)`), even for a correct password. If sign-in succeeds but the follow-up `fetch("/api/auth/session")` fails, the cookie is cleared again, `role` is undefined, and the user lands on `/`, signed out. |
| Loading the dashboard | `/admin` fires `/api/employees/doctors`, `/api/reservations` and `/api/patients/duplicates` together (the date picker's month counts load only once its popover opens). Each one runs a session check and then its own query, and the duplicates scan reads every patient with a reservation count. |

**Confirmed: transaction mode is safe for this app.**
- `adapter-pg`'s `performIO` passes `{ text, values, rowMode, types }` and never a `name`, so every query is an unnamed statement. That is Supabase's own guidance for node-postgres in transaction mode: omit `name`. The `prepared statement … already exists` warning in `Production_Cutover.md` belongs to Prisma's query engine, which this app does not use. **Do not add `?pgbouncer=true`**: that flag is read by the query engine, not by the adapter.
- No session-scoped SQL: no `SET`, advisory locks, `LISTEN` or temp tables in `src/`. The only raw query is the parameterised `SELECT` in `username.ts`.
- All five `$transaction` calls use the batch (array) form. `adapter-pg` runs them as `BEGIN` … `COMMIT` on one checked-out connection, which transaction mode supports.
- `prisma.config.ts` hands the same variable to the Prisma CLI, but production's value is only ever read by the running app. Local `db push` and Studio are unaffected, and **local stays on `5432`**.

**Considered and rejected:**

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| Raise Supabase's Pool Size | Nano's Postgres has few connection slots to spare, and session mode is still the wrong shape for serverless. |
| `idleTimeoutMillis: 5000` (Vercel's Fluid guidance) | In transaction mode an idle client costs one of 200, not one of 15. Every reconnect is a fresh TLS handshake from `iad1` to Ireland, so a shorter idle timeout adds latency for staff who click every few seconds. |
| `attachDatabasePool` from `@vercel/functions` | Not in `package.json` (Hard Rule 1). Revisit only if, after P2, the pooler's client count creeps upward over a day. |
| Re-check status less often than every request | Weakens TJ-007's "immediately". Each check is a primary-key lookup, and once the pool has room it is not the bottleneck. |
| Drop `SessionExpiryNotice`'s own fetch | It duplicates `SessionProvider`'s, so removing it halves tab-return checks. Minor once P2 lands; filed in *Notes for the planner*. |
| Move functions to `dub1` | Declined 2026-08-23 and not reopened here. It would shorten every query, and so how long each connection is held. |

**Steps.** P1–P4 are the user's. P5 is the planner's.

- **P1. Confirm the mode.** Open one full "max clients" line in Vercel's logs. `in session mode` or `pool_size: 15` confirms this pass. If it reads `max client connections reached` (the 200 limit) instead, **stop**: production is already in transaction mode, the cause is a leak, and TJ-063 needs a new pass.
- **P2. Switch production to the transaction pooler.** Supabase → the project → **Connect** → **Transaction pooler**. Copy the URI: host `aws-1-eu-west-1.pooler.supabase.com`, port **`6543`**, user `postgres.<project-ref>`. Host, user and password are the same as today; only the port differs. Replace `[YOUR-PASSWORD]` with the database password and add nothing else to the string. Then in Vercel → Settings → Environment Variables, edit `DATABASE_URL` (Production) and paste. **Never paste the value into a chat.**
  - **If nobody knows the password:** resetting it in Supabase breaks production immediately, until the new string is pasted and deployed. Do it outside clinic hours, and put the new value in local `.env` as well, which has been stale since 2026-08-28.
- **P3. Redeploy:** Deployments → the latest Production deployment → ⋯ → **Redeploy**. Only a new deployment sees an environment change.
- **P4. Check it live:**
  - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://therapyjo.com/api/public/blog` returns `200`. That route runs an `updateMany` and a `findMany`, so a write and a read both went through the new string.
  - Sign in to `/admin` once.
  - Through the next clinic day, Vercel's logs show **no** `max clients`, `EMAXCONN` or `prepared statement` lines.
  - **Rollback:** Instant Rollback to the previous deployment, which keeps its old value.
- **P5. Planner:** record the measured mode and port in `Production_Cutover.md`, in the *Declined, deliberately* row and in Hazard 8's "The ceiling is not tight".

- **The scheduled 15:17 check never ran.** The session restarted, and session-only jobs don't survive that. The check was run by hand once Chrome was reconnected. The close-out `cc15523` was held until then, because Vercel Hobby's Instant Rollback reaches only the previous production deployment.

- **Branch:** `bugfix/db-failure-keeps-session`, cut from `master`.
- **Why:** See TJ-063. Three changes, all about the database connection:
  - **Switch the app's runtime pool to the transaction pooler.** This is the fix for the outage.
  - **Keep sessions alive through a failed status check.** Any database failure (a pooler restart, a Supabase blip, a full pool) otherwise signs out every staff member whose tab refetches the session.
  - **Time out waiting for a connection** instead of waiting forever.

**Revision, 2026-10-26: the port switch moves into code.** TJ-063's P2 needed the database password pasted into Vercel's `DATABASE_URL`. That value is marked Sensitive, so it cannot be read back and edited, and an agent may not type a password. Measured in Supabase's Connect dialog: the transaction pooler differs from the session pooler **only by port**. Rewriting `:5432` to `:6543` on the pooler host, inside `prisma.ts`, therefore makes exactly P2's switch, and the secret is never read, copied or retyped. Two side effects, both wanted:
- No one can bring the outage back by pasting a session-pooler string later.
- Local development's runtime moves to transaction mode too, which `Production_Cutover.md` already recommended.

The Prisma CLI is not affected: `prisma.config.ts` reads the raw variable, and `prisma/seed*.ts` build their own pools from it.

**Decision, answered:**
- **Q1. When the status check cannot reach the database, keep the session or end it?** **Answer: keep it** (user, 2026-10-26).
  - **Keep it (recommended).** An outage signs nobody out. A resigned user is revoked on the next read that reaches the database, and while it is unreachable every route that serves clinic data fails anyway, so they reach nothing.
  - **End it (today's behaviour).** TJ-007's revocation stays strict even during an outage, at the cost of signing the whole clinic out.

**Planning pass:** 2026-10-26, the same pass as TJ-063. Also confirmed:
- `pg-pool` 3.11.0 `connect()`: with `connectionTimeoutMillis` set, a wait for a busy client rejects with `timeout exceeded when trying to connect`, and a new connection attempt is ended with `Connection terminated due to connection timeout` (measured below). Without it, neither has a timer.
- **Ordering hazard.** The timeout on its own would make sign-outs *more* frequent: a request that would have waited and then succeeded now fails, and a failed status check clears the cookie. So the two changes ship together. Never `prisma.ts` alone.
- House style: `src/lib` logs as `console.error("[tag] …", err)` (`audit.ts`), comments explain the why and cite the task, 4-space indent. `tsconfig.json` has `strict: false`.
- The revocation line `if (!current || current.status !== "ACTIVE") return null;` stays byte-identical, so TJ-007 still holds whenever the database answers.

Change no Vercel or Supabase setting, and open neither dashboard. **Never run `prisma db push`, `db seed` or Studio, and never point a probe at the Supabase database.** Runtime verification against production is waived (standing directive, 2026-09-15); the local probes below are not.

**Instructions:**

1. `src/lib/auth.ts`, inside `async jwt({ token, user })`. Replace this anchor, verbatim:

   ```ts
               const current = await prisma.user.findUnique({
                   where: { id: userId },
                   select: { status: true },
               });
               if (!current || current.status !== "ACTIVE") return null;
   ```

   with:

   ```ts
               // A failed lookup is not a revoked account. Letting it throw
               // signs the user out: @auth/core's session action catches the
               // error and clears the session cookie, exactly as it does for
               // a null return. So a full pooler or a database blip would sign
               // out every staff member whose tab refetches the session, and
               // they could not sign back in for the same reason. Keep the
               // session instead; the next read that reaches the database
               // re-checks it. Every route that serves clinic data needs that
               // same database, so a resigned user gains nothing meanwhile.
               // (TJ-063a)
               let current: { status: string } | null;
               try {
                   current = await prisma.user.findUnique({
                       where: { id: userId },
                       select: { status: true },
                   });
               } catch (err) {
                   console.error("[auth] status check failed; keeping the session:", err);
                   return token;
               }
               if (!current || current.status !== "ACTIVE") return null;
   ```

2. `src/lib/prisma.ts`. Replace this anchor, verbatim:

   ```ts
   function createPrismaClient() {
       const pool = new pg.Pool({
           connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
           ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },
           max: 3,
       });
   ```

   with:

   ```ts
   // Supabase's session pooler (port 5432) gives every open client one of
   // only 15 slots at Nano, busy or idle, and a busy clinic afternoon ran
   // out: "(EMAXCONNSESSION) max clients reached in session mode - max
   // clients are limited to pool_size: 15", 71 times in the pooler logs on
   // 2026-10-25. The transaction pooler is the same host, user and password
   // on port 6543, and holds a slot only while a query runs. Switch to it
   // here rather than in the Vercel variable: that value is marked Sensitive
   // and cannot be read back, and doing it in code means a pasted
   // session-pooler string can never bring the outage back. A URL already on
   // 6543, a direct connection and localhost all pass through unchanged.
   // Only this runtime pool switches: prisma.config.ts hands the raw variable
   // to the Prisma CLI, which stays in session mode. (TJ-063a)
   function transactionPoolerUrl(url: string): string {
       return url.replace(/@([^@/?#]+\.pooler\.supabase\.com):5432(?=[/?#]|$)/, "@$1:6543");
   }

   function createPrismaClient() {
       const pool = new pg.Pool({
           connectionString: transactionPoolerUrl(process.env.DATABASE_URL!),
           ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },
           max: 3,
           // pg-pool waits for a connection with no time limit by default.
           // When the pooler is full, a request then hangs until the pooler
           // itself rejects it, and staff see a frozen page. Give up after
           // 10 seconds instead: far longer than a healthy connect, and far
           // shorter than the pooler's own queue. (TJ-063a)
           connectionTimeoutMillis: 10000,
       });
   ```

   Leave `max: 3` and `idleTimeoutMillis` alone; TJ-063 says why. The rewrite touches only the `host:port` after the last `@`, so the userinfo, and with it the password, is never re-encoded.

3. `.env.example`. Replace these three lines, verbatim:

   ```
   # src/lib/prisma.ts opens a pg.Pool per instance; on a serverless host the
   # direct connection exhausts Postgres connection slots under load.
   ```

   with:

   ```
   # Use Supabase's POOLED string (host *.pooler.supabase.com), not the direct
   # one. Session pooler (port 5432) or transaction pooler (port 6543) both
   # work: src/lib/prisma.ts moves the app's own pool from 5432 to 6543 by

   # CLI (db push, Studio, seeds) reads this variable as written, through
   # prisma.config.ts, so keep 5432 here for it.
   # Do not add ?pgbouncer=true: the app reaches Postgres through Prisma's pg
   # driver adapter, which never names its statements.
   ```
